His temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), pulse is 124/min, and blood pressure is 160/102 mm Hg. He is unable to answer questions. His neck is supple. The abdomen is soft and nontender. A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his sister because of increasing confusion for 10 hours. Mental status examination shows psychomotor agitation alternating with lethargy. She says that he has a history of excessive drinking, and she thinks that he has also experimented with illicit drugs.

An x-ray of the chest shows an air-fluid level in the left side of the chest, partial collapse of the left lung, and elevation of the stomach bubble. A 16-year-old boy is admitted to the emergency department because of a knife wound to the left side of his chest. The mediastinum is in the midline.

A 72-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit for pain management and observation of ventricular ectopy 4 hours after undergoing uncomplicated left total knee replacement. Medical history is remarkable for coronary artery disease, for which he takes atorvastatin, furosemide, carvedilol, lisinopril, and 81-mg aspirin. Physical examination discloses no unexpected abnormalities. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 96%. Vital signs now are temperature 38.0°C (100.4°F), pulse 90/min, respirations 16/min, and blood pressure 130/90 mm Hg. He is receiving fentanyl via systemic patient-controlled analgesic pump for pain management. Baseline echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 0.20.

Examination shows dry skin and a nontender thyroid gland that is enlarged to two times its normal size. A 67-year-old woman has had fatigue, dry skin, brittle hair, swelling of the ankles, and cold intolerance for 1 year; she has gained 9 kg (20 lb) during this period. The relaxation phase of the Achilles reflex is greatly prolonged. She appears lethargic. Her pulse is 55/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. There is mild edema of the ankles bilaterally.

At today's visit, she reacts angrily when the issue of contacting the child's father for testing is raised. She states that he abandoned them and that he has no interest in his child. The relationship between the parents is hostile. A 2-year-old boy is brought to the office by his mother for follow-up of a chromosome analysis done 1 month ago. The child has minor dysmorphic features, and growth and developmental delay. Chromosome analysis showed a small unbalanced chromosome translocation, with extra chromosomal material at the tip of chromosome 3. She refuses to cooperate in contacting the father, who could be a translocation carrier. You do not know the father, but an office worker told you that he lives in a nearby town. The mother has been tested and has normal chromosomes without evidence of translocation. The cytogenetics laboratory requested blood samples from both parents for follow-up studies. The parents are divorced, and the mother has custody of the child. The mother says that he is living with a new girlfriend.

She has been treated with amoxicillin for the past 5 days for left otitis media. A 3-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of fever and left ear pain for 3 days. There is edema and tenderness behind the left ear. Otoscopic examination shows a red, dull, left tympanic membrane that does not move. Examination shows the left ear displaced forward and laterally from the head. Her temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 80/60 mm Hg.

Three sets of blood cultures from different sites were obtained. Cardiology, cardiac surgery, and infectious disease physicians were consulted. A 61-year-old man with a history of hypertension presented to the emergency department with a 1-day history of fever, dyspnea, and generalized weakness. He was diaphoretic and had poor dentition. His vital signs were temperature, 38.4°C (101.1°F); blood pressure, 94/40 mm Hg; heart rate, 116/min; and respiratory rate, 26/min. A bedside transthoracic echocardiogram was performed, the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit, and a transesophageal echocardiogram was obtained (Figure 1).Transesophageal echocardiogram obtained from the patient in diastole on the midesophageal long-axis view. A bisphosphonate drug is prescribed. A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician because of low back pain for 1 week. A DEXA scan shows decreased bone mineral density. X-rays of the spine show a compression fracture of L1-2. Menopause occurred 10 years ago. Serum calcium and phosphorus concentrations and serum alkaline phosphatase activity are within the reference ranges. Physical examination shows localized tenderness over the lumbar spine after movement.

Three days later, she has a marked increase in shortness of breath while walking up a flight of stairs. A 72-year-old woman who has smoked 20 cigarettes daily for the past 38 years begins using eyedrops for glaucoma.

Vital signs are temperature 38.3°C (100.9°F), pulse 90/min, respirations 19/min, and blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg. A 38-year-old man with Down syndrome and severe mental retardation is brought to the emergency department by ambulance because of increasing lethargy for the past several hours. Complete blood count shows a leukocyte count of 18,000/mm3 with 23% band neutrophils. On physical examination the patient is awake but lethargic. Auscultation of the chest discloses clear lungs; cardiac examination discloses a systolic click. You do not know if he takes any medications. The patient refuses lumbar puncture for examination of cerebrospinal fluid. The patient's caregiver, who is also the patient's guardian, cannot be located and staff at the group home where the patient resides cannot be reached by telephone. Serum electrolyte concentrations are normal. Toxicologic screening of the urine is negative. Neurologic examination shows decreased muscle tone. The patient is noncommunicative and you are unable to obtain an initial history of his present illness or a past medical history.

She says that she needs the morphine to treat her pain, but she is worried that she is becoming addicted. She is receiving intravenous morphine via a patient-controlled pump. She has no history of substance use disorder. After being severely beaten and sustaining a gunshot wound to the abdomen, a 42-year-old woman undergoes resection of a perforated small bowel. Thirty-six hours postoperatively, she is awake but not completely alert. During the operation, plastic reconstruction of facial fractures, and open reduction and internal fixation of the left femur are also done. She drinks one to two glasses of wine weekly.

Chvostek and Trousseau signs are present. A 57-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of cramping in his hands and feet and numbness and tingling around his lips and in his fingers; these symptoms occurred intermittently for 6 months but have been progressively severe during the past 2 weeks. His serum calcium concentration is 6.5 mg/dL. The abdomen is nontender. Deep tendon reflexes are 4+ bilaterally. His pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 105/65 mm Hg. He also has had a 13-kg (30-lb) weight loss and bulky, foul-smelling stools that do not flush easily. He appears cachectic and chronically ill. He has a 10-year history of drinking 8 to 10 beers daily. He has been hospitalized twice for severe abdominal pain 4 and 6 years ago.

She and her husband live on a farm 90 miles from the nearest dialysis facility. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, a long history of hypertension, and chronic renal failure presumed secondary to diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Serum creatinine concentration on admission was 6.0 mg/dL. Reversible causes of renal failure have been excluded. She is a retired seamstress. A 78-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital for replacement of her left knee joint due to degenerative joint disease. Her current therapy includes a low-sodium, low-protein American Diabetes Association (ADA) diet, enalapril, and acetaminophen. She underwent a tonsillectomy at age 9 years and a laparoscopic cholecystectomy at age 68 years.

She says that she is more fatigued than she was at 65, but she still gardens and drives to the grocery store.

Pelvic examination shows a 4 x 3-cm, tender, fluctuant mass medial to the left labium majus compromising the introital opening. A previously healthy 27-year-old nulligravid woman comes to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of moderate-to-severe pain and swelling of the left labia. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 92/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 115/75 mm Hg. She is sexually active and uses condoms inconsistently.

A previously healthy 24-year-old woman who is a college student comes to the office because of a 6-month history of abdominal bloating, upper abdominal discomfort, and constipation. A urease breath test result is negative. The symptoms are more severe when she is preparing for examinations but improve after bowel movements. She takes no medications. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. A complete blood count and serum electrolyte concentrations are within the reference ranges. She drinks alcoholic beverages occasionally. Physical examination, including digital rectal examination, shows no other abnormalities.

The history and physical examination disclose no abnormalities. This is her first episode of urticaria and it has occurred and then resolved several times in the past week. A 22-year-old woman comes to the office because of urticaria.

His vital signs are within normal limits.

Examination shows no abnormalities. He has been stung by bees three times over the past year, and each reaction has been more severe. The pupils are pinpoint and react sluggishly to light. Examination shows cool, damp skin. A 15-year-old boy is brought to the office by his mother because he has been tired and irritable for the past 3 months. Medical history is unremarkable and he takes no medications.

An endometrial biopsy specimen shows regular tubular endometrial glands with abundant mitotic figures in the endometrial glands and stroma. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 75/min, respirations are 13/min, and blood pressure is 115/79 mm Hg.

Examination of synovial fluid obtained via joint aspiration shows that it is clear, with positively birefringent rhomboids observed under polarized light microscopy. Her hemoglobin concentration is 11 g/dL, and serum ferritin concentration is 140 ng/mL. Her pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 110/90 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities.

X-ray of the abdomen is obtained and shows a 4-cm nail in the left upper quadrant.
